obligations.note: The base catalog fixes the approved DTI ceiling at 40%, but the change sets Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT and mortgage.dti_max_percent to 43. The cited credit committee minutes CP-2026-31 are not in the packet, and the catalog is not updated, so the code no longer equals the approved value.
Ticket CHG-24721 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-12, before review. Its components (mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests, mortgage.controls-data) cover all three touched paths.
Declan Farrell is a baseline-mortgage change_approver and is not the author (Wen Li). He gave a code_review approval.
The code_review approval names head commit 15bde01f, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims ci-runner-07 on the head commit, but the JUnit reports come from host dev-laptop-7.local. They are timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-20. They are not credible as the change's CI run on the final commit. A CRD-1 control test that reads the edited params file would also not show conformance to the approved 40%.
controls/mortgage/policy-params.json is a protected path, and this change alters an approved policy value there. There is no control_owner approval from outside lending-eng.
The register has no exception covering the CRD-1 deviation (DTI ceiling above the approved 40%).

Ledger entry ACR-0406 (CRD-1 proof, premise DTI_MAX_PERCENT = 40) covers Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT, which this change alters, so the entry lapses. No new evidence of the same exhaustive strength is provided.

summary: The change raises the auto-approve DTI ceiling to 43%, while the approved catalog value at base is 40%, so CRD-1 is violated. The change edits an approved policy value in a protected controls file with no control_owner approval. It also lapses the CRD-1 proof without replacement. The CI reports are inconsistent with the claimed run: they come from a personal host and are dated after the review time. Ticket, independent code review and approval coverage are in order, but the change must be rejected.
